title: Pulse (Memory)
markdown:
**What it is:** The Executive's running memory and heartbeat — the decisions it has made with you, the initiatives it's tracking, the advice it has gathered, and the rhythm of work it runs on its own.

**What it does:**

- Browse past **decisions** with their rationale and outcome.
- Track **initiatives** as planned, active, paused, or completed.
- Review **advice** collected from specialists, labelled by domain.
- See your **corrections** — facts you corrected or asked the Executive to keep, where you said them, and what they replaced. They hold everywhere: every conversation, brief, scheduled run and alert review.
- See the **heartbeat** — the recurring cadence of daily briefs, department check-ins, system scans, and pending scheduled follow-ups.
- Keep **your notes**: what you said, in chat and in replies you approved. Each person sees only their own notes; the owner can't see anyone else's.
- See **Done for you**: what the Executive did for you this month, counted from the record (only the owner sees the count), then the last few things it did on its own, each with a line on what came of it.
- See how it is **learning**: after a chat goes quiet, the Executive checks its own answers from your words and your reactions (a correction, a 👎, a reply you stopped, a turn you asked again). The ones that fell short are listed with what you wanted instead and a link to the conversation. Each person sees their own. The owner also sees the ones from channels and group chats, never a teammate's own chat with the Executive, which stays theirs as it does everywhere else. Under the misses, **What it learned**: one line per lesson, in your own words, that the Executive keeps from a miss (a term you use, something you always want included, a thing to do rather than promise, which specialist to ask). It reads a lesson on later chats about the same thing and keeps count of how those went; one that doesn't help stops on its own and is listed under **Stopped saying it**. **Forget** stops one by hand. A lesson applies to the chats of the person it was learned from; one the owner taught it in a channel or group chat applies to everyone's, and is marked so. At the top, the proof: **of the things that went wrong in the last 30 days, how many would go right today**. Each night the Executive replays its misses with everything it has learned since, in a dry run nobody receives (it reads for real but sends, books and saves nothing), and a judge says whether each would now go right. A miss that now passes is marked so with the date; one that depends on what that day's calendar or inbox held is kept as evidence only. A lesson that doesn't fix its miss after two tries, or that twice breaks a chat you had given a thumbs up, stops on its own.
- Edit or delete any item to keep the Executive's memory accurate.

**How to use:**

1. Just chat. Decisions, initiatives and advice are pulled out of your conversations automatically after each chat — there's nothing to add by hand.
2. Click **Pulse** in the sidebar. The **Heartbeat** card shows the last 90 days beside three numbers: what it did today, how long until the next thing it does, and how many days in a row it has been active. **More detail** opens the rest. Below it, under **What it remembers**, a tile for **Decisions**, **Projects**, **Advice**, **Facts you taught it**, **Your notes** and **Learning** opens that list on its own screen; **Pulse** at the top takes you back. Then **Coming up** lists the next few briefs, check-ins and follow-ups (**Full schedule** shows them all, with background scans under **Show background scans**; choose **Cancel follow-up** in a follow-up's **⋯** to drop it), and **Done for you** opens with this month's count in one line (owner only; click it for every count by month or week, against the period before), then lists the last few things it did, each saying what came of it, with **Read it** where it wrote something up and **See changes** on a day it kept your contacts up to date (**All activity** shows the full feed).
3. Choose **Edit** in any row's **⋯** menu to correct it — fix a decision's summary, rationale or outcome, change its domain or tags, change a project's title, summary or status (*planned*, *active*, *paused*, *completed*), or fix an advice item's question, advice or domain — then **Save**.
4. Choose **Delete** in the same menu to remove something that's simply wrong. It asks first; this can't be undone.
5. On **Your notes**, search with **Search your notes**, and use a note's **⋯**: **Correct**, **Pin** / **Unpin**, **Don't remember this** (forgets every note from that conversation and never notes it again) or **Forget** (deletes that one note). Both ask first and can't be undone.
6. On **Learning**, a **This week** card shows your numbers: answers checked this week, how many fell short, lessons kept, and how many of the last 30 days' misses would go right today. **How it learns** opens the four steps (you chat, it looks back 30 minutes later, it keeps a lesson, it checks itself each night). Below it, **What fell short** and **What it learned** switch between the misses and the lessons. Misses are grouped under **Something to learn** (a term, a fact or a preference would have fixed it) and **Couldn't do it** (a tool failed, or it was asked for something it can't do yet); pick one of those chips to see only that kind. Click a row to see what it said, what you wanted and **See the conversation**. To clear several at once, tick their boxes (or **Select all**, or **Select the N that are fixed** for the ones that would go right today; on lessons, **Select the N not helping**) and choose **Forget** (**Stop saying** for lessons). **Undo** brings them back for a few seconds; after that a forgotten miss is gone. Retired lessons are under **Show N stopped**.
7. To correct a fact, just say it in chat — *"Maple House is 48 units, not 52"* or *"we're 42 people now"*. The Executive keeps it (a company-profile field such as headcount or burn updates the profile too), and it shows under **Facts you taught it** with your words. Choose **Retire (stop using it)** in a correction's **⋯** menu when it no longer holds (it asks first); a company-profile change is fixed on the Company profile instead. Older, retired and declined versions stay under **Show history (N)**. You can also email a correction from your own address: nothing changes until you reply CONFIRM to the confirmation email the Executive sends you. Teammates on your People list can correct facts too, from the web app or their own Slack or Discord. Theirs are marked with their name and wait for your approval at the top of that list with **Approve** and **Decline** (the tile says how many), and they appear in your morning brief. Under **Teammates' corrections**, untick **needs my approval** next to a teammate you trust to let theirs apply straight away; one that would replace yours still waits for you. Only you can retire someone else's correction.

**Example:** tell the Executive *"we've decided to push the EU launch to Q2 so we can finish SOC 2 first."* Afterwards, **Pulse → Decisions** shows that decision with its rationale. If it captured the wrong reason, edit it — future answers build on what's recorded here.

**Just for yourself?** When you use Open Executive just for yourself, the heartbeat leaves out department check-ins and the "Awaiting people" list, and the count of active projects takes the department check-ins' place under **More detail**. The same projects appear on Home under **Your projects**.

*Note: this memory is searchable across the system, so what's captured here informs future answers.*
